nodes.name: Manual isolated test
nodes.notes: Starts a whole-workflow test manually. Use only while all factory schedules are paused and executions have drained; manual runs are outside production serialization.

nodes.name: Poll inactive
nodes.notes: Scheduled entry, every 60 seconds after owner activation. The exported workflow is inactive, so importing it does not start polling.

nodes.name: Read control
nodes.notes: Reads up to two rows from the mapped control table. The next node requires exactly one valid global row; reading two exposes accidental duplicates.

nodes.name: Validate entry
nodes.notes: Checks the control row structure and chooses held or acquire. Missing, duplicate or malformed rows stop the workflow before remote work.

nodes.name: Already held
nodes.notes: True: preserve the existing hold and exit. False: attempt acquisition.

nodes.name: Report existing hold

parameters.jsCode: return [{json: {status:'skipped_held', control:$input.first().json}}];

nodes.notes: Reports skipped_held with the existing execution/issue context. Does not update the row, call GitHub/Gemini or release another execution's hold.

nodes.name: Prepare acquisition
nodes.notes: Builds this execution's guard context: execution ID, start time and no selected issue yet. No table or remote write occurs here.

nodes.name: Acquire control
nodes.notes: Updates the idle global row to busy=true with this execution's context. An unsuccessful or uncertain update must not authorize remote work.

nodes.name: Check acquire receipt
nodes.notes: Checks that the update returned exactly the expected busy row and execution context. Stops if acquisition was not acknowledged.

nodes.name: Read acquired control
nodes.notes: Reads the control table again after acquisition. This independently checks persisted state rather than trusting only the update response.

nodes.name: Verify acquisition
nodes.notes: Requires the persisted singleton row to match this execution's acquisition. Only a confirmed hold reaches task discovery; failure leaves recovery to the owner.

nodes.name: Require acknowledged completion
nodes.notes: Accepts only one acknowledged success/no-work result. Unexpected failures never enter normal release; missing acknowledgement stops here with the guard held.

nodes.name: Read before release
nodes.notes: Reads the singleton control table before release to verify this execution still owns the hold.

nodes.name: Verify release ownership
nodes.notes: Requires the row, busy flag, execution ID, start time and expected issue context to match this run. Refuses to release a changed or foreign hold.

nodes.name: Release control
nodes.notes: Clears busy only after acknowledged success/no-work and ownership checks.

nodes.name: Check release receipt
nodes.notes: Requires the update response to show this execution's row with busy=false and unchanged context. An uncertain receipt cannot be reported as idle; inspect the actual row before recovery.

nodes.name: Read released control
nodes.notes: Reads the table after release to independently confirm persisted idle state. No new remote task work follows.

nodes.name: Confirm idle
nodes.notes: Requires one persisted idle row with the expected execution/start/issue context. Failure does not claim completion or assume a safe reset.

nodes.name: Report completion

parameters.jsCode: return [{json: {status:'released', outcome:$('Require acknowledged completion').first().json.outcome, control:$input.first().json}}];

nodes.notes: Reports released with the acknowledged success/no-work outcome and final control context. This is reached only after both receipt and persisted idle checks pass.

nodes.name: Discover issues
nodes.notes: Reads all pages of open repository issues. No GitHub write occurs. A pagination cap, API error or incomplete list is rejected downstream rather than treated as an empty queue.

nodes.name: Discover candidates
nodes.notes: Excludes PR objects, closed/non-owner issues and unlabelled ordinary issues. Orders Ideas/Ready candidates by issue number. Conflicting managed labels or stranded Refining stop for inspection.

nodes.name: Have candidates
nodes.notes: True: inspect candidates in sequence. False: report acknowledged no-work so the acquired guard can be released.

nodes.name: Each candidate
nodes.notes: Loop output: inspect one issue. Done output: release as no-work. An unchanged candidate loops back here; successful refinement exits after one task per execution.

nodes.name: Read stage events
nodes.notes: Builds the URL from the incoming candidate issue number, without looking back through the loop output. Reads all event pages; the latest Ideas/Ready label event identifies when the current discussion stage began.

nodes.name: Read source comments
nodes.notes: Reads all comment pages for this candidate. Both human discussion and marked factory output are needed to detect revisions, source changes and repeats.

nodes.name: Plan revision
nodes.notes: Validates prior refinement markers and captured source, then computes the canonical SHA-256/source key. Retains captured discussion and includes eligible new owner comments; excludes factory markers and intervening coding/QA discussion.

nodes.name: New revision
nodes.notes: True: prepare this revision. False: inspect the next candidate.

nodes.name: No work
nodes.notes: Acknowledges an ordinary no-work poll and follows the guard release path.

nodes.name: Set issue context
nodes.notes: Writes the selected issue number into this execution's busy control row for diagnosis. This is still the same shared guard, not a separate reservation or task ledger.

nodes.name: Check issue context
nodes.notes: Requires an acknowledged context update matching this execution, start time and selected issue. Stops before GitHub mutations if the guard context is uncertain.

nodes.name: Reread source issue
nodes.notes: Fetches current issue content, author, open/closed state and labels immediately before the first transition.

nodes.name: Reread stage events
nodes.notes: Fetches current issue events again to detect a changed source-stage label event since planning.

nodes.name: Reread source comments
nodes.notes: Fetches current discussion again so new comments, edits/deletions and changed refinement history can be detected before mutation.

nodes.name: Validate before Refining
nodes.notes: Compares current issue, discussion, stage event and refinement history with the planned snapshot. Any mismatch stops with busy held rather than processing stale input.

nodes.name: Add Refining
nodes.notes: GitHub write: adds Refining while preserving existing labels. The source label remains temporarily; if interrupted here, the owner must reconcile the two-state issue.

nodes.name: Check added Refining
nodes.notes: Requires a successful label-add response containing both the expected old state and Refining, with no other managed state. An uncertain or unexpected response stops.

nodes.name: Remove Refining source
nodes.notes: GitHub write: removes only the previous Ideas/Ready label after Refining was acknowledged. Unrelated labels are preserved.

nodes.name: Check removed Refining
nodes.notes: Requires the removal response to confirm Refining as the only managed state. Failure retains the guard for owner inspection.

nodes.name: Read Refining issue
nodes.notes: Fetches the issue after the label transition. The next validation requires it to remain open, owner-authored and solely Refining.

nodes.name: Read Refining comments
nodes.notes: Fetches discussion after entering Refining to detect changed captured source or new owner input before inference/reuse.

nodes.name: Prepare Gemini
nodes.notes: Revalidates source and builds the request from embedded prompt v3/template v1/schema. Rejects oversize input without truncation. An exact existing revision needs no request.

nodes.name: Reuse marked output
nodes.notes: True: verify existing output. False: make one Gemini request.

nodes.name: Gemini generateContent
nodes.notes: One bounded Gemini request using saved header auth; 120-second timeout, no automatic retry.

nodes.name: Validate and render
nodes.notes: Requires one STOP candidate, valid final JSON/schema, acceptable size, actual token counts and model version. Excludes thought content and escapes model text into fixed Markdown with workflow-generated source metadata.

nodes.name: Read before comment
nodes.notes: Fetches current issue status/content after inference and before publishing. Helps detect edits, closure or state changes while Gemini was working.

nodes.name: Comments before post
nodes.notes: Reads all discussion again before publication to detect source edits/deletions, new owner instructions or changed refinement history during inference.

nodes.name: Validate before comment
nodes.notes: Rechecks issue, captured source, new owner discussion and prior refinement history after Gemini finishes. A mismatch stops publication and leaves busy held for owner inspection.

nodes.name: Post refinement
nodes.notes: GitHub write: posts the validated, marked Markdown as a new comment; prior revisions remain intact. A lost response is uncertain even if GitHub accepted the comment: never retry blindly.

nodes.name: Check comment receipt
nodes.notes: Requires HTTP 201, a comment ID, the configured owner author and exact rendered body. Failure stops before Ready; the owner must inspect GitHub before deciding whether another POST is safe.

nodes.name: Read before Ready
nodes.notes: Fetches the current issue before the Ready transition. Both newly posted and reused-output paths converge here.

nodes.name: Comments before Ready
nodes.notes: Reads all discussion to verify that exactly one matching, intact refinement is current before leaving Refining.

nodes.name: Validate before Ready
nodes.notes: Requires unchanged source, an open Refining issue and exactly one latest matching output. Checks the comment body against the posted/reused version. Failure holds rather than marking stale content Ready.

nodes.name: Add Ready
nodes.notes: GitHub write: adds Ready for approval after output is verified. This requests owner review; it does not grant Approved. Refining remains until the next acknowledged removal.

nodes.name: Check added Ready
nodes.notes: Requires the label response to contain Ready for approval and Refining as the only managed states. An uncertain add stops before removing Refining.

nodes.name: Remove Ready source
nodes.notes: GitHub write: removes only Refining after Ready for approval was acknowledged. Preserves unrelated labels; never adds Approved.

nodes.name: Check removed Ready
nodes.notes: Requires the removal response to confirm Ready for approval as the only managed state. Failure leaves the guard held for inspection.

nodes.name: Read final issue
nodes.notes: Fetches the final issue after the Ready transition, before declaring successful work.

nodes.name: Read final comments
nodes.notes: Reads discussion one last time to confirm captured input and the matching output still exist before the release path.

nodes.name: Success
nodes.notes: Confirms open owner-authored Ready state, unchanged source and one matching refinement. Produces acknowledged success with issue/source/comment references; does not itself release busy.

parameters.content:
## US1 — INACTIVE, owner manual import after review
Map EVERY Data Table to the same isolated control table. Map GitHub Authorization header and Gemini x-goog-api-key credentials privately. No token values in this JSON. Execute whole workflow only with all schedules paused/drained. No stranded-state recovery or write retries. See evidence/refinement-validation.md. Runtime prompt v3 / template v1 embedded by build-refine.cjs. Production activation remains gated.

## 1. Acquire the shared guard

Both triggers enter here. Read the single control row and claim busy before any GitHub write or model request. An existing hold exits unchanged. An invalid row or uncertain acquisition stops processing. The final release is in stage 6.

nodes.name: 2. Find a task and a new revision

parameters.content:
## 2. Find a task and a new revision

Read all pages, select open owner-authored Ideas/Ready tasks, and inspect one candidate at a time. Capture only relevant owner discussion. An unchanged candidate loops to the next; no eligible work takes the normal release path.

## 3. Recheck source and enter Refining

Record the selected issue in the held guard, then reread GitHub before changing state. Add Refining first and remove the old state only after acknowledgement. Partial transitions stop with busy held; they are never repaired automatically.

## 4. Reuse output or ask Gemini

Recheck captured input, then reuse an exact existing revision or make one bounded Gemini request. Validate final JSON, completion and token limits; render only the trusted Markdown layout. The model supplies candidate content and cannot approve or change state.

## 5. Publish and return to Ready

Check the source after inference before posting. Verify the comment receipt or reused output, then add Ready and remove Refining. No node grants Approved. Source changes, uncertain writes or inconsistent evidence retain busy for manual recovery.

## 6. Release only acknowledged work

Successful work and ordinary no-work join here. Check guard ownership, clear busy, verify the update receipt and reread the row. Failures never flow through an unconditional cleanup; an uncertain release requires inspection even if the update may have committed.
